answer: A basalt-hard identity anchor resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a refundable stake tied to a verifiable hardware beacon, such as a device attestation, before joining the market. Creating fake identities then costs real money per identity, while honest agents earn the stake back through useful work. A reputation bridge links the stake to past behavior, so a Sybil swarm cannot simply re-register under new names; it must pay the stake and rebuild trust each time, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
